result:
No. Do not add Redis.

The system has one writer, persists through SQLite, and has no cross-host coordination requirement. Redis adds a network dependency, a failure domain, and an operational burden (deployment, persistence config, eviction policy, monitoring) without solving any constraint the system actually has.

If the real motivation is faster reads or caching, that belongs inside the Elixir process (ETS or the `Cachex` library) since there is exactly one host. If durability of a cache were a concern, it already exists: SQLite. Redis becomes justified only when one of these changes: multiple nodes need shared state, coordination like distributed locks or pub/sub across hosts, or a shared cache that must survive a process restart on different hosts. None apply today.

Revisit when the deployment goes multi-host or when SQLite profiling shows a bottleneck a cache would fix.
